sense.text:
“On the first day of the first month shalt thou set up the tabernacle of the tent of the congregation.” At that time it was not called the temple. It was called the tabernacle, and it had several meanings: it was symbolic of what was to come, of what would come down from heaven, and of the new bodies Israel would get.

That is why there are four temples in Jerusalem and not five: the first tabernacle was portable. We had it when we came out of Egypt, and we carried it with us the forty years we wandered.

“In the first month in the second year, on the first day of the month, that the tabernacle was reared up.” We set the tabernacle up and moved around with it. In it the Lord had us make the menorah, the seven-branched candlestick.

“Thou shalt put into the ark the testimony which I shall give thee.” The Lord was going to give Moses a testimony. People think Moses was on the mountain forty days and forty nights just to get the ten commandments, but it does not take forty days to get ten commandments.

It would take that long to get the testimony from Genesis up to the time Israel was in the wilderness: the Lord explaining creation to Moses from let there be light, the first day through the seventh, the sabbath given to us, Adam and Eve put out of the garden, their children, and all that history. That is what the Lord gave Moses in those forty days.

A mercy seat of pure gold, and “two cherubims of gold, of beaten work”, one on each end of the mercy seat. “The cherubims shall stretch forth their wings on high, covering the mercy seat with their wings, and their faces shall look one to another.” God himself commanded Moses to make two angels, with their faces toward each other and their wings stretched out, and set them on the ark of the covenant.

“There I will meet with thee, and I will commune with thee from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubims which are upon the ark of the testimony.” The Lord already gave Moses the law against graven images, and in the same breath told him to make two images of cherubims, which are angels, and put them on the ark. That was not unlawful. The key was not to bow down to them and worship them.

“Thou shalt make a candlestick of pure gold”: this is the menorah. “Six branches shall come out of the sides of it; three branches of the candlestick out of the one side, and three branches of the candlestick out of the other side.” One main candlestick, three branches on one side and three on the other: the seven-branched menorah. Not eight, not nine. The Bible tells you exactly how many it is, if you read.

precepts.why:
Read right after the Lord told Moses to make the two cherubims: “Take ye therefore good heed unto yourselves; for ye saw no manner of similitude on the day that the Lord spake unto you in Horeb out of the midst of the fire: lest ye corrupt yourselves, and make you a graven image”, the likeness of male or female, of any beast, of any winged fowl, of any thing that creepeth, of any fish. Then: “lest thou lift up thine eyes unto heaven, and when thou seest the sun, and the moon, and the stars, even all the host of heaven, shouldest be driven to worship them, and serve them.”

He said this in Deuteronomy 4 and in Exodus 20, and still he commanded images of angels on the ark. Nobody finds that strange, because the point was never the image: it was being driven to worship and serve it.

That is why these scriptures matter today. Certain Christians who hate black images suddenly found Deuteronomy 4 and Exodus 20 about graven images when they saw a black Christ. All the years they had the white Jesus they never saw those scriptures. That is suspicious.

“Take this book of the law, and put it in the side of the ark of the covenant of the Lord your God, that it may be there for a witness against thee.”

Not only did the Lord give Moses the testimony of creation and the history from let there be light to the time of Moses; he was also giving Moses the law. That took time, and that is what was being done in those forty days. All that Moses wrote down was put in the side of the ark of the covenant as a witness against us.

sense.text: “The first covenant had also ordinances of divine service, and a worldly sanctuary”: a sanctuary made by man. “There was a tabernacle made; the first, wherein was the candlestick, and the table, and the shewbread; which is called the sanctuary.”

“After the second veil, the tabernacle which is called the Holiest of all”: the holy of holies, where the ark of the covenant was. Only the high priest was allowed in there. The people could not just walk in where the ark was and have a conversation.

In it were “the golden censer, and the ark of the covenant overlaid round about with gold, wherein was the golden pot that had manna, and Aaron’s rod that budded, and the tables of the covenant”: the two tablets.
“And over it the cherubims of glory shadowing the mercyseat; of which we cannot now speak particularly.” Paul did not want to speak at that time about what the ark with the two cherubims symbolized.

precepts.why:
“The Lord reigneth; let the people tremble: he sitteth between the cherubims; let the earth be moved. The Lord is great in Zion; and he is high above all the people. Let them praise thy great and terrible name; for it is holy.”

This is what the ark symbolized. What the Lord instructed Moses to build, the two cherubims on the ark with the mercy seat in the middle, is a figure of the kingdom in the heavens, the true heaven: the Lord sitting on his throne between two huge cherubims with their wings stretched out.

We can only imagine how terrible that scene looks; in truth we cannot imagine it. That is why it says to praise his “great and terrible name”.

sense.text:
“After the number of the days in which ye searched the land, even forty days, each day for a year, shall ye bear your iniquities, even forty years.” When the Lord sent the spies into the land, they came back with an evil report, all but Joshua and Caleb. Joshua and Caleb said the giants are in the land, we can take them, God is with us. The others said we are scared, we can’t do it, and they put fear on all Israel.

They spied out the land in fear and dread for forty days, so God gave them a year for every day: “your children shall wander in the wilderness forty years, and bear your whoredoms, until your carcases be wasted in the wilderness.” Then Israel got their nerve up and said we are going in anyway; Moses told them not to go because the Lord was not with them, and they got beaten. That is why we wandered forty years with the portable tabernacle.

“Then Solomon began to build the house of the Lord at Jerusalem in mount Moriah, where the Lord appeared unto David his father, in the place that David had prepared in the threshingfloor of Ornan the Jebusite.” This is where the temples begin: the first temple in Jerusalem, built under king Solomon in mount Moriah.

precepts.why:
David assembled the princes, the captains and the mighty men to Jerusalem and said, “I had in mine heart to build an house of rest for the ark of the covenant of the Lord”. “But God said unto me, Thou shalt not build an house for my name, because thou hast been a man of war, and hast shed blood.” Everybody has a position. David’s lot was to be a man of war; he killed a whole lot of people to get the land of Israel and the twelve tribes together. It was not for David to build the house.

The Lord chose David over all his big, burly brothers, “for he hath chosen Judah to be the ruler”, and of all David’s sons “he hath chosen Solomon my son to sit upon the throne of the kingdom of the Lord over Israel.” See what Israel is called: the kingdom of the Lord. We are the kingdom of the Lord.

Then God says, “Solomon thy son, he shall build my house and my courts: for I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father.” That is deep. A lot of people don’t know who Solomon is. Notice that when all the prophets come back, Solomon is never mentioned; this is why.

“Moreover I will establish his kingdom for ever, if he be constant to do my commandments and my judgments”. Solomon’s kingdom did not last forever, so he is speaking of something more about Solomon.

“The days that David reigned over Israel were forty years: seven years reigned he in Hebron, and thirty and three years reigned he in Jerusalem. Then sat Solomon upon the throne of David his father; and his kingdom was established greatly.” David reigned forty years in all, and Solomon took his throne.
“The time that Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel was forty years.” Forty years under David, forty under Solomon. That has everything to do with the temples, as Deuteronomy 28 shows.

“If thou shalt hearken diligently unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe and to do all his commandments which I command thee this day, that the Lord thy God will set thee on high above all nations of the earth: and all these blessings shall come on thee, and overtake thee”. Blessed in the city and in the field, the fruit of thy body, thy ground, thy cattle, thy basket and thy store, coming in and going out; “they shall come out against thee one way, and flee before thee seven ways.”

All these blessings came upon us under king David and king Solomon, and only for eighty years: forty under David, forty under Solomon. After Solomon his son Rehoboam took over, the kingdom split, and that is when all hell started to break loose.

The blessings of Deuteronomy 28, verses 1 through 14, are coming back again when Christ returns, and then we are going to get the fullness of them.

sense.text:
“In the four hundred and eightieth year after the children of Israel were come out of the land of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon’s reign over Israel, in the month Zif, which is the second month, that he began to build the house of the Lord.” This verse is very heavy if you slow down. Solomon began to reign around 970 BC. Go back 480 years before that and you have the time Israel came out of Egypt, around 1450 BC. BC time goes backwards, from high numbers down to one.

The month Zif is the second month: May.

The house was threescore cubits long, twenty broad and thirty high: a large temple. A cubit is the length from the elbow to the tip of the middle finger, anywhere from about eighteen to twenty inches. Chambers were built round about against the walls, “the nethermost chamber was five cubits broad, and the middle was six cubits broad, and the third was seven cubits broad”.

“The house, when it was in building, was built of stone made ready before it was brought thither: so that there was neither hammer nor axe nor any tool of iron heard in the house”. Hiram built a lot of it for Solomon and then had it transported to him.
“They went up with winding stairs into the middle chamber, and out of the middle into the third.” The temple had winding stairs. He finished it and covered it with beams and boards of cedar.

“If thou wilt walk in my statutes, and execute my judgments, and keep all my commandments to walk in them; then will I perform my word with thee, which I spake unto David thy father: and I will dwell among the children of Israel, and will not forsake my people Israel.” “So Solomon built the house, and finished it”, between 970 and 930 BC.

precepts.why:
Verse 1 speaks of the children of Israel coming out of Egypt, when the Lord destroyed those Egyptians who chased us. And they were black. People say we make this about black and white; no. The Egyptians were black, and God did not choose them. Sheba was black, and God did not choose them. The Ethiopians were black, and God did not choose them. Our people are scattered in those lands today, but this is speaking of the pure bloods back then.

“I am the Lord thy God, the Holy One of Israel, thy Saviour: I gave Egypt for thy ransom, Ethiopia and Seba for thee.” That Egypt was a black, dusty nation; Seba is Somalia. Three black nations that God destroyed for us. “Since thou wast precious in my sight, thou hast been honourable, and I have loved thee”: he does not love everybody, he does not love all black people; he said I have loved thee, Israel.

“Therefore will I give men for thee, and people for thy life.” God is saying, I will kill people because I love you. You have not seen love like that. This is the scripture for those who say we teach that all black people will be saved; nobody ever said that.

sense.text:
This is inside the temple: the molten sea. “It stood upon twelve oxen, three looking toward the north, and three looking toward the west, and three looking toward the south, and three looking toward the east”. Great lavers with water in them, set on images of oxen. The priests went above it and washed their hands up to the elbow; there were continual baptisms there.

And the brim was “wrought like the brim of a cup, with flowers of lilies”: images of lilies, too.

On the borders of the ten bases of brass “were lions, oxen, and cherubims”. God wanted images of lions, of oxen, and of cherubims, which are angels, in his house.

This is the same God who said in Deuteronomy, I don’t want images of things in heaven or on earth to bow down to. The key is to bow down and worship, and that is the part they miss. They worship a white image of Jesus, then condemn us for having images that show what was in the temple. God instructed Solomon to put images in the temple.
On the plates and borders “he graved cherubims, lions, and palm trees”. Cherub angels, lions and palm trees, all by God’s design.
“After this manner he made the ten bases: all of them had one casting, one measure, and one size. Then made he ten lavers of brass”, each laver set on one of the bases.

The temple is built. Solomon gathered the elders and the heads of the tribes “that they might bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord out of the city of David, which is Zion.” All Israel is at the temple, within and without, and Solomon makes his prayer.
“Solomon stood before the altar of the Lord in the presence of all the congregation of Israel, and spread forth his hands toward heaven”. He was standing: one form of prayer.

We are in this prayer today. “If they sin against thee, (for there is no man that sinneth not,) and thou be angry with them, and deliver them to the enemy, so that they carry them away captives unto the land of the enemy, far or near”. Some of our people were taken far from Jerusalem, as far as the South Pacific; some are nearer, like those in Madagascar, Ghana and the Afro-Egyptians.

“Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives, and repent”. To repent is to change your ways and keep the commandments; that is the fullness of the word. Christians leave out the second part: they say change your ways and call on his name, and then tell you that you can now celebrate Christmas.

“We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness”. To say you have sinned you must know what sin is: breaking God’s laws. Perverse means a twisting of what is right, against God’s law and design: distorted speech, morally corrupt actions, a twisted mindset that rejects righteousness and truth. That is the black community, black and brown and Latino.

Every person has to go before the Lord himself and say what he has done that was perverse; nobody can go for you. More than one sexual partner is perverse. A same-sex partner is perverse. Dealing with an animal is perverse. And wickedness is so broad it covers the drug use, the weed, the hookah. You had better say, we have sinned and have done perversely.

“And so return unto thee with all their heart, and with all their soul, in the land of their enemies, which led them away captive, and pray unto thee toward their land, which thou gavest unto their fathers, the city which thou hast chosen”. That is why we say face Jerusalem, not face the east: from the Sudan, Jerusalem is to the north. We pray toward the land and the city he chose.

When Solomon had made an end of praying, “he arose from before the altar of the Lord, from kneeling on his knees with his hands spread up to heaven.” He went from standing to kneeling: two forms of prayer. “And he stood, and blessed all the congregation of Israel with a loud voice”, saying “there hath not failed one word of all his good promise, which he promised by the hand of Moses his servant.”

precepts.why: “Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law.” To say “We have sinned” in the prayer of verse 47, you have to know what sin is. Sin is breaking God’s laws.

“Is the law sin? God forbid. Nay, I had not known sin, but by the law: for I had not known lust, except the law had said, Thou shalt not covet.”

So to confess your sins you must be studying the Bible. If you are not studying, you will not know what is right and what is wrong. You will not just wake up one day and know what you did wrong.

“Then went out to him Jerusalem, and all Judea, and all the region round about Jordan, and were baptized of him in Jordan, confessing their sins.”

No church does that. You will not find a church today doing water baptism with the people confessing their sins. You can be baptized seven times, going from this church to that church, and never once be made to confess anything: just dipping in water and it’s all good in Jesus. They are not following what the scripture says at all. To confess your sins you must have studied the scriptures and be able to say, I broke this law: thou shalt not covet, I am guilty; thou shalt not commit adultery, I am guilty; thou shalt not steal, I am guilty. That is what verse 47 calls for.

sense.text:
After Solomon died, his son Rehoboam took over and the kingdom split in two: the kingdom of Judah and the kingdom of Israel. Christians like to leave out that history. Ask them what happened to the northern kingdom of Israel and nobody knows; they just disappeared. So when they get to the Gentiles in the New Testament, they say that is everybody.

“The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles”. That gives you the hint of hints: the northern kingdom was being called Gentiles. Once you read on about the Gentiles getting salvation, it should tell you that is the northern kingdom.

After king Hezekiah, Babylon made three campaigns against Judah. Assyria had taken the northern kingdom, and Babylon conquered Assyria, so Babylon held the northern kingdom and came against Judah back in the land: Jehoiachin captured; Zedekiah set up as a puppet king, who rebelled, so Nebuchadnezzar came back; then Jerusalem destroyed. Nebuchadnezzar and them were Kushites, the ancient Ethiopians.

We were terrible in the land. This is what king Josiah had to do: “he brought out the grove from the house of the Lord, without Jerusalem, unto the brook Kidron, and burned it at the brook Kidron, and stamped it small to powder”.

“He brake down the houses of the sodomites, that were by the house of the Lord, where the women wove hangings for the grove.” You had the temple there, and sodomite houses, brothels, right next to it.

And the women wove the hangings for them. That is why today women always have some gay best friend they want to introduce you to and have take care of their kids. Women are the ones making the extravagant, evil outfits for these sodomites; women bring their kids around that life and then wonder why they turn out like that. Sisters should not have a gay best friend taking care of their kids.

“He brought all the priests out of the cities of Judah, and defiled the high places where the priests had burned incense, from Geba to Beer–sheba”. Josiah had to get rid of those Levites. They allowed these homos to set up brothels next to the temple and said nothing; they were wandering around with them lighting incense. He had to bring new priests in.

“Nevertheless the priests of the high places came not up to the altar of the Lord in Jerusalem, but they did eat of the unleavened bread among their brethren.” They did not want to change their lives. They would not come up.

How bad were we? “I will cause them to eat the flesh of their sons and the flesh of their daughters, and they shall eat every one the flesh of his friend in the siege and straitness”. When Babylon came against us it got so bad we resorted to cannibalism. Babylon circled Jerusalem and let no food in. We think it only happened under Rome, but it happened under Babylon first.

precepts.why:
“Through the anger of the Lord it came to pass in Jerusalem and Judah, till he had cast them out from his presence, that Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.” This is the puppet king rebelling against Nebuchadnezzar.

Then Nebuchadrezzar “came, he and all his army, against Jerusalem, and pitched against it, and built forts against it round about. So the city was besieged unto the eleventh year of king Zedekiah. And in the fourth month, in the ninth day of the month, the famine was sore in the city, so that there was no bread for the people of the land.” No bread for the people of the land: that is when we resorted to eating our sons and daughters, as Jeremiah 19:9 said.

sense.text: “As I was among the captives by the river of Chebar, that the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God.” Ezekiel was taken into captivity, and from there he was shown the visions of God, including how bad we were.

precepts.why: “By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down, yea, we wept, when we remembered Zion.” King David wrote this, and it is the same captivity Ezekiel was in by the river of Chebar. This is what David saw in the spirit long before it happened.

sense.text: “As I sat in mine house, and the elders of Judah sat before me”. The elders of Judah in captivity came and sat down in front of Ezekiel, as if they were so righteous and had done nothing wrong.

The Lord “put forth the form of an hand, and took me by a lock of mine head; and the spirit lifted me up between the earth and the heaven, and brought me in the visions of God to Jerusalem”, where was “the image of jealousy, which provoketh to jealousy.”

“Seest thou what they do? even the great abominations that the house of Israel committeth here, that I should go far off from my sanctuary?” He dug through the hole in the wall, and “Go in, and behold the wicked abominations that they do here.” The Lord was about to show Ezekiel what these men sitting before him had been doing.

“Every form of creeping things, and abominable beasts, and all the idols of the house of Israel, pourtrayed upon the wall round about.” All kinds of idols were painted inside the temple, with sodomite houses right next door. Seventy of the ancients of Israel stood before them with censers, and Jaazaniah in the midst.

“Hast thou seen what the ancients of the house of Israel do in the dark, every man in the chambers of his imagery? for they say, The Lord seeth us not; the Lord hath forsaken the earth.” That is what a lot of brothers and some sisters believe today: that he isn’t watching.

“There sat women weeping for Tammuz.” Tammuz was the son of Semiramis, the reincarnation of Nimrod. That history carried all the way down, and today they call him baby Jesus: Tammuz died as a child and they worship him in child form. Roman Catholicism made Jesus the forever baby, always in Mary’s arms. The women say, this is just for the children; no, it is not.

In the inner court, between the porch and the altar, “about five and twenty men, with their backs toward the temple of the Lord, and their faces toward the east; and they worshipped the sun toward the east.” They were not praying toward the temple; they turned their backs to it. Be careful, you face-the-east brothers: that is what they were doing here.

“They have filled the land with violence, and have returned to provoke me to anger: and, lo, they put the branch to their nose.” They would light the branch and get high from it, like the weed people smoke today to feel good and tingly. God was angry with them then, and he is angry with you today. Those who say the weed opens visions to them are seeing the devil; they are opening portals to Satan.

“Therefore will I also deal in fury: mine eye shall not spare, neither will I have pity: and though they cry in mine ears with a loud voice, yet will I not hear them.” God told Ezekiel he would kill these people for being so wicked while sitting before him as if they were righteous.

“Cause them that have charge over the city to draw near, even every man with his destroying weapon in his hand.” Six men came with slaughter weapons, and one among them “clothed with linen, with a writer’s inkhorn by his side”: the Lord called to that angel.

“Set a mark upon the foreheads of the men that sigh and that cry for all the abominations that be done in the midst thereof.” To sigh and cry for the abominations, you must know the law. It has always been about his law, from Genesis to Revelation; you can tap dance your way around it, but his law will still be there.

If you were not marked, not sealed with God’s law: “Go ye after him through the city, and smite: let not your eye spare, neither have ye pity”. Smite means kill. The angels moving through with the Babylonians were told not to spare.

“Slay utterly old and young, both maids, and little children, and women”: old Israelite men and women, young men and young women, little children. And women, set off on their own, because women always think they get a pass. Do not think what we read here won’t happen again.

“But come not near any man upon whom is the mark; and begin at my sanctuary. Then they began at the ancient men which were before the house.” Begin at my sanctuary: start with those men.

precepts.why: “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” That is what God is looking for: the law sealed among his disciples. The ones who sigh and cry over the abominations are the ones who know his law.

The mark of Ezekiel 9:4 is the same thing as Revelation 7:4: “I heard the number of them which were sealed: and there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.” Sealed means marked: marked with God’s law.

“For the time is come that judgment must begin at the house of God: and if it first begin at us, what shall the end be of them that obey not the gospel of God?” Ezekiel 9 said begin at my sanctuary; Peter says judgment begins at us, the men and women who know the scriptures.

Why start with us? Because we know better; we know the law. We are quick to point the finger at people on the street: look how she wears pants, look at him smoking weed, look at him watching porn. How many of us still smoke weed, still watch porn? How many women still secretly celebrate Christmas for the children, still go to Thanksgiving?

sense.text:
“What thing shall I take to witness for thee? what thing shall I liken to thee, O daughter of Jerusalem?” Nothing can be compared to what happened to us. Not the Moabites, not the Syrians: no nation went through what the Israelites went through.

People say everybody was a slave at one time. Not like we were. Everybody did not lose their identity; everybody’s families were not destroyed; everybody’s culture and heritage was not changed. The East Indians and the Chinese here had indentured servitude, worked a limited time, got paid and got set free, and kept their language and culture.

“For thy breach is great like the sea: who can heal thee?” Our breach between us and the Lord is great like the sea.

“Thy prophets have seen vain and foolish things for thee”: Christmas, Kwanzaa, Mother’s Day, Father’s Day, white Jesus. “They have not discovered thine iniquity, to turn away thy captivity”: they never told us we went into slavery because we broke God’s laws. They say God moves in mysterious ways. If breaking the commandments led us into captivity, keeping the commandments, in the faith of Christ, is the way out; they never tell us that.

“But have seen for thee false burdens and causes of banishment.” Divorce because the man forgot an anniversary or could not afford a diamond ring. Going broke every Christmas buying for the kids, the coworkers, the mamas and papas; a new suit and white shoes every Easter; boiling the eggs for the egg hunt. These are burdens because none of those holidays are of God.

“All that pass by clap their hands at thee; they hiss and wag their head at the daughter of Jerusalem, saying, Is this the city that men call The perfection of beauty, The joy of the whole earth?” The tour buses through Harlem pointing at the people, wanting to rub the children’s hair. They put us in human zoos, with signs not to feed the animals; the last of them closed only about sixty years ago. Is this who they called the city of God? At one time we were the joy of the whole earth; look how far we have fallen. They destroyed the empires and the pyramids of the Americas so no remnant would show that these people once ruled the earth.

“All thine enemies have opened their mouth against thee”, speaking evil against us. “We have swallowed her up: certainly this is the day that we looked for”: we have swallowed up the twelve tribes; this is what we waited for all our lives, to get rid of the Israelites.

“The Lord hath done that which he had devised; he hath fulfilled his word that he had commanded in the days of old”. He warned us, as in Deuteronomy 32, what was going to happen; we did not believe Moses, and it came to pass centuries later. “He hath set up the horn of thine adversaries”: he set up our enemies as kings.

“Let tears run down like a river day and night: give thyself no rest”. “Pour out thine heart like water before the face of the Lord: lift up thy hands toward him for the life of thy young children”. That is what the Lord wants us to do: cry, just cry before him.

“Shall the women eat their fruit, and children of a span long?” A span long: tiny babies. The women were eating their babies. “Thou hast killed, and not pitied”; “in the day of the Lord’s anger none escaped nor remained”. Nobody got away.

precepts.why:
“They that be slain with the sword are better than they that be slain with hunger: for these pine away, stricken through for want of the fruits of the field.” The sword is a quick death; hunger is a slow death.

“The hands of the pitiful women have sodden their own children: they were their meat in the destruction of the daughter of my people.” Their children were their food. That is the women eating their fruit in Lamentations 2:20.

sense.text: Babylon came against us, but watch who helped Babylon. “Shall I not in that day, saith the Lord, even destroy the wise men out of Edom, and understanding out of the mount of Esau?” That is future prophecy: every one of the mount of Esau cut off by slaughter.
Why? “For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever.” They committed violence against us.

“In the day that thou stoodest on the other side, in the day that the strangers carried away captive his forces, and foreigners entered into his gates, and cast lots upon Jerusalem, even thou wast as one of them.” When the Babylonians came against us, Esau stood on the other side and would not let us escape. God says Edom was just like the Babylonians to us.

“Thou shouldest not have looked on the day of thy brother in the day that he became a stranger”. We did become strangers; the strangers of Ephesians 2:12 are us. “Neither shouldest thou have rejoiced over the children of Judah in the day of their destruction”: our brother Esau was happy when Babylon came against us. “Neither shouldest thou have spoken proudly in the day of distress.”

“Thou shouldest not have entered into the gate of my people in the day of their calamity”. When Babylon came in, Esau came in with Babylon, and “laid hands on their substance”: they stole our holy things, just as Babylon did.

“Neither shouldest thou have stood in the crossway, to cut off those of his that did escape”. The people who did escape, Esau caught and dragged to the Babylonians, and “delivered up those of his that did remain in the day of distress.”

precepts.why:
David saw this whole thing. “Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem; who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof.” Raze it, destroy it: that is what it means when Obadiah says they spoke proudly against us.

David calls Edom “O daughter of Babylon, who art to be destroyed”, because they were helping the Babylonians, and prophetically they are going to be destroyed. “Happy shall he be, that rewardeth thee as thou hast served us”: what they did to us, let it come back on them.

“Happy shall he be, that taketh and dasheth thy little ones against the stones.” That lets us know that when Edom helped Babylon, they were grabbing our babies and smashing them against the stones. David lived in a time of prosperity, yet he saw this.

How could David see it? “Let me freely speak unto you of the patriarch David, that he is both dead and buried, and his sepulchre is with us unto this day. Therefore being a prophet”. David was not just a king; he was a king and a prophet. That is how he could see and write down visions like Psalms 137, and many more.

“Rejoice and be glad, O daughter of Edom, that dwellest in the land of Uz; the cup also shall pass through unto thee: thou shalt be drunken, and shalt make thyself naked.” Jeremiah tells Edom to be glad because the cup we had to drink, they are going to drink.

“The punishment of thine iniquity is accomplished, O daughter of Zion; he will no more carry thee away into captivity”. Prophetically Jeremiah tells Israel the punishment is accomplished: there is a cutoff date for our captivity, and we are approaching it. This is the last captivity.

“He will visit thine iniquity, O daughter of Edom; he will discover thy sins.” Once this chain of events is broken for us, it is Edom’s turn: all the evil they did to us comes right back on them. That is the shame and the cutting off of Obadiah 1:10.

sense.text: Jeremiah wrote Lamentations about all that took place under Babylon. “In the fifth month, on the seventh day of the month, which is the nineteenth year of king Nebuchadnezzar”, Nebuzar–adan the captain of the guard came to Jerusalem: “and he burnt the house of the Lord, and the king’s house, and all the houses of Jerusalem, and every great man’s house burnt he with fire.”

“The pillars of brass that were in the house of the Lord, and the bases, and the brasen sea that was in the house of the Lord, did the Chaldees break in pieces, and carried the brass of them to Babylon.” The pots, shovels, snuffers, spoons, firepans and bowls, the gold and the silver: Babylon stripped everything in the temple and the great houses. The temple Solomon built was burned and destroyed.

Now the second temple, rebuilt by Zerubbabel the governor and Joshua the high priest. Persia conquered Babylon, which held Assyria as well. “The Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia”, and Cyrus proclaimed, “he hath charged me to build him an house at Jerusalem, which is in Judah. Who is there among you of all his people? his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem”.

“Whosoever remaineth in any place where he sojourneth, let the men of his place help him with silver, and with gold”. We were there seventy years; we built houses and everything. Some Israelites said, we are going to stay; we are not going back to Jerusalem.

“Then rose up the chief of the fathers of Judah and Benjamin, and the priests, and the Levites, with all them whose spirit God had raised, to go up to build the house of the Lord”. And Cyrus brought forth the vessels Nebuchadnezzar had taken out of the house of the Lord and numbered them to Sheshbazzar the prince of Judah. They were allowed to take everything back.

precepts.why:
Acts 2 proves who stayed behind in the lands where they sojourned. “There were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.” They all marvelled: “are not all these which speak Galileans? And how hear we every man in our own tongue, wherein we were born?”

Now see where these Jews were born. “Parthians, and Medes”: Persia and Media, modern Iran. “Elamites”: India and Pakistan. “The dwellers in Mesopotamia”: Iraq, Babylon. Cappadocia, Pontus, Asia, Phrygia and Pamphylia: modern Turkey, where the Assyrian Empire was. “In Egypt, and in the parts of Libya about Cyrene”: Africa. “Strangers of Rome, Jews and proselytes”: a proselyte is a convert back to the law of Moses. “Cretes and Arabians”: Greece and Arabia.

So it is proven: some of the Israelites stayed in those lands, just as Ezra 1:4 speaks of whoever remained where he sojourned.

sense.text: “When the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin heard that the children of the captivity builded the temple unto the Lord God of Israel”: adversaries means enemies. They came saying, “Let us build with you: for we seek your God, as ye do”, since the days the king of Assyria brought them there (2 Kings 17).

“Ye have nothing to do with us to build an house unto our God; but we ourselves together will build unto the Lord God of Israel”. They had the wisdom to say no. This was not an all-inclusive thing; it was meant for our people and our people only.

“Then the people of the land weakened the hands of the people of Judah, and troubled them in building, and hired counsellors against them, to frustrate their purpose, all the days of Cyrus king of Persia, even until the reign of Darius”. For years nothing got built because they hired counsellors against us.

precepts.why:
1 Esdras tells the same history in more detail: “It is not for us and you to build together an house unto the Lord our God. We ourselves alone will build unto the Lord of Israel”.

“But the heathen of the land lying heavy upon the inhabitants of Judea, and holding them strait, hindered their building; and by their secret plots, and popular persuasions and commotions, they hindered the finishing of the building all the time that king Cyrus lived: so they were hindered from building for the space of two years, until the reign of Darius.”

Secret plots, popular persuasions to sway the people, commotions: for two years not one brick was laid.

sense.text: What happened in those two years? “In the second year of Darius the king” the word came by Haggai to Zerubbabel the governor and Joshua the high priest: “This people say, The time is not come, the time that the Lord’s house should be built.” They were saying that because of the secret plots, popular persuasions and commotions that hindered them.

“Is it time for you, O ye, to dwell in your cieled houses, and this house lie waste?” God did not send Haggai to play with them. You are a governor, you are a high priest, you live lovely in your homes, but look at God’s house: you haven’t put a brick to it.

“Consider your ways. Ye have sown much, and bring in little; ye eat, but ye have not enough”, “and he that earneth wages earneth wages to put it into a bag with holes.” Everything you have, you are going to lose; you have been losing it, and now I am telling you why.
“Go up to the mountain, and bring wood, and build the house; and I will take pleasure in it, and I will be glorified, saith the Lord.”

“When ye brought it home, I did blow upon it. Why? saith the Lord of hosts. Because of mine house that is waste, and ye run every man unto his own house.” God himself blew on what they brought home. Some of us can relate: we work for Esau or have our own businesses, we bring in little, and we are confused why things keep going wrong. It is because you are not putting your bricks in here.

“The heaven over you is stayed from dew, and the earth is stayed from her fruit”: no blessings from heaven or earth, and a drought on the land, the corn, the wine, the oil, men, cattle and all the labour of the hands.

“Then Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest, with all the remnant of the people, obeyed the voice of the Lord their God, and the words of Haggai the prophet”. They did not say, I am over you. They took heed, because they knew it was the word of the Lord. “I am with you, saith the Lord.” And the Lord stirred up their spirits, “and they came and did work in the house of the Lord of hosts”.

precepts.why:
“Who is left among you that saw this house in her first glory? and how do ye see it now? is it not in your eyes in comparison of it as nothing?” You would have to be very old: they had been away seventy years. Who still alive remembers the temple Solomon built, before Babylon destroyed it? Compared with what Solomon built, what they were building was nothing.

Yet: “be strong, O Zerubbabel, saith the Lord; and be strong, O Joshua, son of Josedech, the high priest; and be strong, all ye people of the land, saith the Lord, and work: for I am with you”.

“The elders of the Jews builded, and they prospered through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah the son of Iddo.” Not only Haggai but Zechariah was prophesying to them. “And they builded, and finished it”, “and this house was finished on the third day of the month Adar, which was in the sixth year of the reign of Darius the king.” Adar is the twelfth month, February. The second temple was rebuilt.

sense.text: After Persia, Greece came in, under Antiochus Epiphanes. “The king had sent letters by messengers unto Jerusalem and the cities of Juda that they should follow the strange laws of the land, and forbid burnt offerings, and sacrifice, and drink offerings, in the temple; and that they should profane the sabbaths and festival days”. They set up idols and sacrificed “swine’s flesh, and unclean beasts”: pig on the altar, in the temple, and more unclean beasts besides.

“That they should also leave their children uncircumcised”, “to the end they might forget the law, and change all the ordinances.” That was their goal. “And whosoever would not do according to the commandment of the king, he said, he should die.”

precepts.why: Still what the Greeks did: “the temple was filled with riot and revelling by the Gentiles, who dallied with harlots, and had to do with women within the circuit of the holy places, and besides that brought in things that were not lawful.” They brought whores into the temple and had sex there. That is the polluting of the sanctuary.

sense.text: Chapter 4 is the cleansing of the temple and the rededicating of the altar. “He chose priests of blameless conversation, such as had pleasure in the law”. That is who your circle has to be. If you want things to get better, change your circle. Fringes and a border of blue don’t make everybody right. Coming in, a man can keep getting in trouble because his circle is idiots: fights on 42nd Street with some clowns, jumping the turnstile and getting arrested. Look around and see it: these are a bunch of idiots, and I am an idiot for being with these clowns. Change your circle, and go be around the elders.

They cleansed the sanctuary and bare out the defiled stones. The altar of burnt offerings the heathen had defiled they pulled down, and laid up the stones “until there should come a prophet to shew what should be done with them.” They said, we must wait for a prophet to show us what to do.

They built a new altar of whole stones according to the law, made new holy vessels, and “into the temple they brought the candlestick”: that is the menorah. They lighted the lamps “that they might give light in the temple”, set the loaves on the table and spread out the veils.

“On the five and twentieth day of the ninth month, which is called the month Casleu”: the ninth month is November. They offered sacrifice according to the law on the new altar. That is the feast of dedication.
“They kept the dedication of the altar eight days and offered burnt offerings with gladness, and sacrificed the sacrifice of deliverance and praise.”

precepts.why:
“It was at Jerusalem the feast of the dedication, and it was winter. And Jesus walked in the temple in Solomon’s porch.” In November it gets cold. Christ kept the feast of dedication in the winter, and walked in the temple because it was a holy convocation.

Then king Herod added to the temple they had built, from 19 BC to 63 AD, continually building to make it more elaborate and fancy.

sense.text: “His disciples came to him for to shew him the buildings of the temple.” Look what Herod did.

“See ye not all these things? verily I say unto you, There shall not be left here one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down.” Then they say the Wailing Wall is the one thing left standing. So the white man is right and the Son of God is wrong? That wall has nothing to do with the temple; it was from Fort Antonia that the Romans built.

Christians will never challenge these fake Jews, Amalek, and call them liars, though the Son of God said not one stone would be left. On the news they say it is the last wall left, and they hump the wall and call it davening, sending spiritual energy into it.

precepts.why: “As some spake of the temple, how it was adorned with goodly stones and gifts”. Herod made it far more beautiful. Christ answered, “the days will come, in the which there shall not be left one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down.” The same word as Matthew 24:2.

“Rise, and measure the temple of God, and the altar, and them that worship therein. But the court which is without the temple leave out, and measure it not; for it is given unto the Gentiles”.

In Herod’s temple you see the temple in the very centre and the courts outside it. Herod added those courts so the Gentiles could come and observe the Jews. They were never part of God’s design, not from Moses, Solomon, or Zerubbabel and Joshua. So the Lord said, don’t measure that; it is for the Gentiles, the real Gentiles.

“And the holy city shall they tread under foot forty and two months.” The temple was destroyed; it is gone.

sense.text: The temple was destroyed in 70 AD after Rome besieged us. “Three shepherds also I cut off in one month”: the scribes, the Sadducees and the Pharisees. “My soul lothed them”: God hated them. “And their soul also abhorred me”: they hated the Lord. Those three groups put Christ on the cross; they turned him over to Pilate for his crucifixion.

“Then said I, I will not feed you: that that dieth, let it die; and that that is to be cut off, let it be cut off; and let the rest eat every one the flesh of another.” Cannibalism happened again. Rome besieged us for seven years and no food was allowed to enter; whatever was already inside was soon done and gone.

precepts.why:
“The Lord shall bring a nation against thee from far, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flieth”: Rome’s symbol was the eagle. “A nation whose tongue thou shalt not understand”: they spoke Latin. “A nation of fierce countenance, which shall not regard the person of the old, nor shew favour to the young.” They showed no favour to the young.

“He shall besiege thee in all thy gates, until thy high and fenced walls come down, wherein thou trustedst”. We trusted in the walls of Jerusalem that Nehemiah built back; we said those walls are not falling, and they fell.

“Thou shalt eat the fruit of thine own body, the flesh of thy sons and of thy daughters”. The man “that is tender among you, and very delicate”, a prince among us, would not give his own family any of the flesh of the children he was eating. And “the tender and delicate woman”, who had servants to carry her and “would not adventure to set the sole of her foot upon the ground”, her eye was evil toward her husband and her children, “for she shall eat them for want of all things secretly in the siege and straitness”.

Everybody says I would never do that. You don’t know what you will turn into when you are starving. Watch when the food assistance really gets shut down: neighbors become enemies overnight.

sense.text: “In your patience possess ye your souls. And when ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh.” “Then let them which are in Judea flee to the mountains”: if you can escape, run. Those in the countries were not to come back in.
“For these be the days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled.” What Moses prophesied in Deuteronomy 28, here the Son of God says will come to pass.

“Woe unto them that are with child, and to them that give suck, in those days!” Because they would be resorting to cannibalism and eating their children. “There shall be great distress in the land, and wrath upon this people.”

“They shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.” If you are in Jerusalem you will be captured and made slaves in all nations, and the real Gentiles will take the land over.

So why read that and then say those in the land are the Jews? The Son of God said the Gentiles would be in the land; CNN says those are the Jews. So Christ is a liar and the white man is right again. The Christian Negro believes everything the white man says and nothing that Christ said.

precepts.why: “Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets”. The part to see here is the prophets. Everything the prophets said, Christ did not come to change or destroy. What the prophets said would happen is going to happen; Christ was there to ensure it gets fulfilled. That is why he says these are the days “that all things which are written may be fulfilled.”

“For as many as are of the works of the law are under the curse: for it is written, Cursed is every one that continueth not in all things which are written in the book of the law to do them.” “The just shall live by faith.” “The man that doeth them shall live in them.”

“Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law”. What Christ did lets us know there is a time limit on the curse. People ask why it didn’t stop right then. He cannot change what the prophets said, because he is the one who gave them the prophecy: he told Moses, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Zechariah and Haggai what to say. He did not come to change it; he came to make sure everything written is fulfilled.

sense.text: Read down from verse 8 to see how the thought flows. “I took my staff, even Beauty, and cut it asunder, that I might break my covenant which I had made with all the people.”

“And it was broken in that day”: 70 AD broke the covenant. “And so the poor of the flock that waited upon me knew that it was the word of the Lord.” The poor of the flock are the followers of Christ. When all of it happened in 70 AD, they understood this was what Christ had prophesied: the destruction, the cannibalism, don’t come back to the land. The high priests and the rest, who believed nothing, were asking why the Almighty was doing this to them.

Besides the portable tabernacle Moses carried, that is two temples gone: the first, Solomon’s, destroyed by Babylon; and the second, rebuilt by Zerubbabel and Joshua and added to by Herod, destroyed by Rome.

The Lord set Ezekiel “in the midst of the valley which was full of bones”, “and, lo, they were very dry.” “Son of man, can these bones live? And I answered, O Lord God, thou knowest.” Only you know, Lord.

“O ye dry bones, hear the word of the Lord.” “I will lay sinews upon you, and will bring up flesh upon you, and cover you with skin, and put breath in you, and ye shall live”. The skin is identity: they are going to get some kind of identity.

“The bones came together, bone to his bone. And when I beheld, lo, the sinews and the flesh came up upon them, and the skin covered them above: but there was no breath in them.” They came together as Christians, they came together as Muslims, and there was no breath in them. Our people try to get some kind of identity, some in Islam, some in Christianity, and it causes disunity, because Christianity and Islam are two of the bloodiest religions that destroyed our race. They have the image of Jesus in their heart; that is not what God is talking about.

The breath is the word of God; it was not in them. There is no breath, no life, in Islam, in Christianity, or in any man-made religion. And the life spoken of is eternal life, rulership, reigning on the earth. Our people in these religions are not going to get it, however many Hail Marys they say.

“Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe upon these slain, that they may live. So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them”: the word of God, the words of Christ, came into them. “And they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army.” That is what John saw, and what Ezekiel saw.

If you were confused about the valley of dry bones, verse 11 explains who they are: “Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel”, all twelve tribes. “Behold, they say, Our bones are dried, and our hope is lost: we are cut off for our parts.”

“I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all”. The two kingdoms made one again under one king.

precepts.why: “The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.” That is the bones with no breath: they have no understanding. One group follows white supremacy and calls it Christianity; another follows the Arabs and calls it Islam; both destroyed us mentally and physically.

“Their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city”. We are not physically dead; we are spiritually dead. The great city is Babylon the Great, the United States of America.

“Which spiritually is called Sodom”: not the real Sodom, but a spiritual Sodom where same-sex relationships are glorified. “And Egypt”: a spiritual Egypt, because just as the twelve tribes were captive in ancient Egypt learning hundreds of gods, so are we here: Nike, Adidas, Gucci, Fendi are gods, and some will kill each other over them. The pyramid and the all-seeing eye are on the back of the dollar bill on purpose. “Where also our Lord was crucified”: a spiritual Jerusalem, where they betray the Son of God and reject his teachings with the same spirit as back then.

They “shall see their dead bodies three days and an half”, three hundred and fifty years, “and shall not suffer their dead bodies to be put in graves”, because they are not physically dead. “They that dwell upon the earth shall rejoice over them, and make merry, and shall send gifts one to another”: they made a holiday over our destruction. Merry Christmas. Christmas is a day of our destruction: Pope Nicholas V, Zwarte Piet, and the transatlantic slave trade that enslaved the black Jews they called Moors.

“Because these two prophets tormented them that dwelt on the earth.” We tormented them when we ruled.

This is the torment of Revelation 11:10 that makes the nations rejoice over our dead bodies. Amaziah “went to the valley of salt, and smote of the children of Seir ten thousand. And other ten thousand left alive did the children of Judah carry away captive, and brought them unto the top of the rock, and cast them down from the top of the rock, that they all were broken in pieces.”

That is torment. That is what we did; that is the history, and they know it: not the peon whites, their elites. And you on the street say, what did we do? Read a book. These people were evil and we treated them evil. They were a vile race, the seed of evildoers, and we treated them the way they deserved to be treated: we pushed that whole group off the cliff, because God said to do it. Then we broke the commandments, and now they have their foot on our neck and will never tell us the true history the Bible tells.

What is the breath? “It is the spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.” To quicken is to change, to convert. Christ’s words are the breath that was not in the bones.
“Keep my commandments, and live”. What gives us life is keeping the commandments.

“This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.” Now we have the understanding of the breath: the law and the word of God bring the dry bones to life.

“After three days and an half the Spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet; and great fear fell upon them which saw them.” After three hundred and fifty years, the same breath Ezekiel spoke of entered into us, and we stood up on our feet as the Israelites, the twelve tribes.

The nations who know the history are very afraid of this awakening, because they know it means the Messiah is soon to come; they time it by the awakening of the twelve tribes. They are not worried about those in the street, or the camps that change their doctrine every day. They are worried about the brothers teaching identity and the commandments across the world.

Paul says the same thing as Ezekiel 37:11. “That at that time ye were without Christ, being aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of promise, having no hope, and without God in the world”. Having no hope: that is “our hope is lost”, cut off for our parts.

“But now in Christ Jesus ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ.” The blood of Christ brings us back together. “For he is our peace, who hath made both one”: both kingdoms, Judah and Israel, one nation, the same thing Ezekiel 37:22 says. Paul got it from Ezekiel. “And hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us”: the animal sacrifice, which Christ did away with.

sense.text: “For the ungodly said, reasoning with themselves, but not aright, Our life is short and tedious”, “neither was there any man known to have returned from the grave.” The ungodly starts with the white man, followed by the other nations, and our people who follow them. They do not believe in Christ or the resurrection.

“Let us oppress the poor righteous man, let us not spare the widow, nor reverence the ancient gray hairs of the aged. Let our strength be the law of justice”. That is why they sit in the courthouses, make the legislation, and put their children in those places to manipulate the laws. “For that which is feeble is found to be nothing worth”: we, the twelve tribes, are the feeble.

“Let us lie in wait for the righteous; because he is not for our turn, and he is clean contrary to our doings”. Those keeping the commandments are opposite to everything society says. “He professeth to have the knowledge of God: and he calleth himself the child of the Lord.” We are the children of God. “He was made to reprove our thoughts”: we were brought back to undo all the lies that bound our people.
“He is grievous unto us even to behold”. That is why they said, we don’t want a black Jesus; make him look like us. “His ways are of another fashion.”

“We are esteemed of him as counterfeits”. They are not the real Jews; they are counterfeits. They are not the real Christians; they are counterfeits. “He abstaineth from our ways as from filthiness”, and “maketh his boast that God is his father.”

And so they want to build a third temple: Amalek wants to destroy the Al-Aqsa mosque and rebuild on the Temple Mount.

“Let us see if his words be true”: “if the just man be the son of God, he will help him”. That is what they did to Christ, mocking him on the cross. “Let us examine him with despitefulness and torture”: what they did to Christ they will do to the followers of Christ. “Let us condemn him with a shameful death”.

precepts.why: “I saw the woman drunken with the blood of the saints, and with the blood of the martyrs of Jesus: and when I saw her, I wondered with great admiration.” This is the shameful death of Wisdom 2:20. There is martyrdom coming; it has not happened yet, but it is coming.

sense.text: They want to build the third temple, and they talk about getting a red heifer, which is mentioned only here: “Speak unto the children of Israel, that they bring thee a red heifer without spot, wherein is no blemish, and upon which never came yoke”. Why the stress on the red heifer? Red: they always look for something red to match them. They have five red heifers, flown over from Texas to Israel, to sacrifice when the temple is rebuilt, and they have to destroy the Al-Aqsa mosque to do it. Let’s wait and see, and see what the Bible says about the third temple.

“I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them”: that is the elect, the men who make it. Judgment given unto them means power given unto them. “The souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus”: the martyrs. They “had not worshipped the beast”, the white man, “neither his image, neither had received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands”: they did not take on or support his sin. “And they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.”

“But the rest of the dead lived not again until the thousand years were finished. This is the first resurrection.” The rest of the dead are the two thirds: some of our own mothers, fathers, sisters and brothers in Christianity and Islam who give us the finger when we try to save their souls, and say no black man is king over them.

precepts.why: “It shall come to pass, that in all the land, saith the Lord, two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein.” Two out of three Negroes and Latinos shall be cut off and die, and the third shall be left. Those two parts are the rest of the dead of Revelation 20:5.

sense.text: “A pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb.” The same thing Ezekiel 47 speaks of. That pure water clear as crystal is the word of God.

“The tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits”: twelve, with the twelve apostles and the twelve tribes. “And yielded her fruit every month”: every month the law of God goes out. The sabbath day, and this month you keep the feast of tabernacles, this month the memorial of blowing of trumpets.

“And the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.” If the nations obey, they will be all right. If they don’t, no rain in their land: famine, drought, death.

“And there shall be no more curse”. When this is established, the third temple, there shall be no more curse on the Israelites. When Christ returns, the curse is over. “But the throne of God and of the Lamb shall be in it; and his servants shall serve him”.

precepts.why: “From one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith the Lord.” Everybody on the planet will be made to come and serve the Lord, keep the sabbath day and keep the new moon. That is the fruit yielded every month.

“Every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles.” Everybody is going to be made to keep these high holy days.

“Whoso will not come up of all the families of the earth unto Jerusalem to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, even upon them shall be no rain.” Got an attitude, don’t want to do what the Lord says? Famine in your land: no rain, no crops, no cattle. “And if the family of Egypt go not up”, “there shall be the plague”. That is what the leaves for the healing of the nations means: obey and be healed, or perish.

sense.text: “Who are these that fly as a cloud, and as the doves to their windows?” When the destruction comes, those that are alive will be in the chariots, looking out of the windows, as Zechariah 13:8 and Psalms 91 go together.
“Surely the isles shall wait for me, and the ships of Tarshish first”: Tarshish is Spain. They bring “thy sons from far, their silver and their gold with them”: the nations bring their wealth.

“The sons of strangers shall build up thy walls”: this is the third temple being built. “And their kings shall minister unto thee: for in my wrath I smote thee, but in my favour have I had mercy on thee.” When Christ returns it is the time of our favour.

“Thy gates shall be open continually”, “that men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles”: their wealth, and their kings brought too. “For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish; yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted.” You will never hear that read in church. Perish means die; wasted means destroyed.

“The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the fir tree, the pine tree, and the box together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary”. That is the third temple. “And I will make the place of my feet glorious.”

“The sons also of them that afflicted thee shall come bending unto thee; and all they that despised thee shall bow themselves down at the soles of thy feet”. They are going to bend the knee. It will not be willing: the prideful nations will be made to get on both knees. “And they shall call thee, The city of the Lord, The Zion of the Holy One of Israel.”

“Whereas thou hast been forsaken and hated, so that no man went through thee”: nobody cared for us or helped us. “I will make thee an eternal excellency, a joy of many generations”: the joy of the earth once again.

“Thou shalt also suck the milk of the Gentiles, and shalt suck the breast of kings”: we will take in their wealth, because it is really ours. “Thou shalt know that I the Lord am thy Saviour and thy Redeemer, the mighty One of Jacob.”

“For brass I will bring gold, and for iron I will bring silver, and for wood brass, and for stones iron”. “I will also make thy officers peace, and thine exactors righteousness.” An exactor is a tax collector. We will tax the world and have the top economy on the planet; all nations must pay tax.

precepts.why: “They heard a great voice from heaven saying unto them, Come up hither. And they ascended up to heaven in a cloud”. That is who fly as a cloud in Isaiah 60:8.

The same thing as Isaiah 60:14, Old Testament and New saying the same: “Behold, I will make them of the synagogue of Satan, which say they are Jews, and are not, but do lie; behold, I will make them to come and worship before thy feet, and to know that I have loved thee.”

Right now it looks like the Lord does not love us; we are at the bottom of society. He says he is going to make the world know that he has loved us.

Christ says the same about the exactors: “Doth not your master pay tribute?” Tribute money is taxes. “Of whom do the kings of the earth take custom or tribute? of their own children, or of strangers? Peter saith unto him, Of strangers.” If you were a Roman citizen you did not pay taxes; America started that way too, then turned on its own poor.

“Jesus saith unto him, Then are the children free.” That is the part people miss: you are free when the nations pay you taxes.

“The city had no need of the sun, neither of the moon, to shine in it: for the glory of God did lighten it, and the Lamb is the light thereof. And the nations of them which are saved shall walk in the light of it: and the kings of the earth do bring their glory and honour into it.” That is collecting taxes: the same thing as Isaiah 60. It has not changed.

sense.text: “For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob”. Right now we are at the bottom, but because of what Christ did, and the covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, he will have mercy on the Israelites. He is not having mercy on everybody on the planet: Jacob is not everybody, and not everybody is Israel. “And set them in their own land: and the strangers shall be joined with them, and they shall cleave to the house of Jacob”: they will be servants, and obey us.

“And the people shall take them, and bring them to their place”. We are going to put all nations back where they belong. The whites in South Africa and in Australia, the Arabs throughout North Africa, Esau and the Chinese throughout the Caribbean: all that mixing and taking over is over when this day comes. “The house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids: and they shall take them captives, whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors.”
“The Lord shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy fear, and from the hard bondage wherein thou wast made to serve”.

precepts.why: “They of the south shall possess the mount of Esau; and they of the plain the Philistines: and they shall possess the fields of Ephraim, and the fields of Samaria: and Benjamin shall possess Gilead. And the captivity of this host of the children of Israel shall possess that of the Canaanites, even unto Zarephath”. We are going to take the land over once again: the twelve tribes set in their own land.

sense.text: “The wilderness and the solitary place shall be glad for them; and the desert shall rejoice, and blossom as the rose.” Them is the Israelites. Right now Lebanon is a wilderness, a solitary place, a desert; it will be glad for us and blossom because we are coming back to the land.

“It shall blossom abundantly, and rejoice even with joy and singing: the glory of Lebanon shall be given unto it”. Who shall see the glory of the Lord? The Israelites: not the Arabs, not the other nations. When we get Lebanon back, it will flourish again.

precepts.why: “Every place whereon the soles of your feet shall tread shall be yours: from the wilderness and Lebanon”. Lebanon was ours from the beginning, and the Arabs are there now. They do not belong there; we are going to put these people where they belong, and the glory of Lebanon given in Isaiah 35:2 is ours.

sense.text: “In the last days it shall come to pass, that the mountain of the house of the Lord shall be established in the top of the mountains, and it shall be exalted above the hills”. Our kingdom is going to be the highest government, exalted above all kingdoms.

“Many nations shall come, and say, Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord”. First it is the scattered Israelites who come; later the nations will be forced to come up and worship the King, as Zechariah 14 said. “For the law shall go forth of Zion”: the law is what will be taught.

“Nation shall not lift up a sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.” The only way there can be peace on earth is when the twelve tribes are reestablished under Christ; otherwise it is war after war. “They shall sit every man under his vine and under his fig tree; and none shall make them afraid”.
“For all people will walk every one in the name of his god”: god with a little g. That is us.

precepts.why: Who is this god? “I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.” Gods with a little g: the children of the Most High. Each people will walk in the name of its god, the Israelite set over them.

“Lord, thy pound hath gained ten pounds. And he said unto him, Well, thou good servant: because thou hast been faithful in a very little, have thou authority over ten cities.” When you have authority over ten cities, you are going to be their god.

“Be thou also over five cities.” Over five cities, you are their god, little g. That is Micah 4:5.

sense.text: Still speaking of the third temple: “For the Father judgeth no man, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son”. Christ is going to do all the judging.

precepts.why: “For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad.” We are all coming before the judgment seat of Christ.

sense.text: “I saw a great white throne, and him that sat on it”: him that sat on it is Christ, “from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away”. He is coming in power.

“I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God; and the books were opened”. This is the rest of the dead, who lived not again until the thousand years were finished, and everybody else. “They were judged every man according to their works.” What are Christians talking about, just have the love of Jesus in your heart and you’re good? Everybody is judged according to their works.

“Death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death. And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.” Whose names are in the book of life?

precepts.why: “At that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people”, “and at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book.” The only ones written in the book are Daniel’s people: the Israelites. Not Moab and Ammon and all the other nations.

Here is a precept for it; get mad if you want. “For I am with thee, saith the Lord, to save thee: though I make a full end of all nations whither I have scattered thee, yet will I not make a full end of thee: but I will correct thee in measure, and will not leave thee altogether unpunished.”

He will make a full end of all nations: their time will be up and they will not be on the planet with us. Esau will be gone first, and the other nations will be there for a time, but then a time will come when the Lord says they are no longer needed. He will not make a full end of Jacob.

sense.text: “Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city.” That speaks of the third temple, and also of the fourth temple.

Paul discussed the true temple, the fourth temple, but in allegory. “We have such an high priest, who is set on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens; a minister of the sanctuary, and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, and not man.” The true tabernacle, which God made and not man.

“There are priests that offer gifts according to the law”: the Levites, “who serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things”. Everything done when the tabernacle and sanctuaries were set up is symbolic. “See, saith he, that thou make all things according to the pattern shewed to thee in the mount.” Everything Moses made was made according to the pattern God showed him.

precepts.why:
The worldly sanctuary again: the candlestick, the table and the shewbread; the Holiest of all with “the ark of the covenant overlaid round about with gold”, the manna, Aaron’s rod and the tables of the covenant, and “the cherubims of glory shadowing the mercyseat”.

Here is the point: “it was therefore necessary that the patterns of things in the heavens should be purified with these; but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these. For Christ is not entered into the holy places made with hands, which are the figures of the true; but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us”.

Christ did not go into the second temple Zerubbabel and Joshua made; those were the figures, the symbols, of the true tabernacle. When the high priest went into the holy of holies, God came down on the mercy seat. Christ entered the true tabernacle, heaven itself, as high priest, and presented himself before the Father.

“I saw in the night visions, and, behold, one like the Son of man came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days, and they brought him near before him.” They brought Christ near before the Father: he went into the true holy of holies. That is the high priest set on the right hand of the throne.

sense.text: We covered the portable temple, then the first, second and third temples. Now the fourth. “After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come.” That is all we want: thy kingdom come. And thy will be done where? On earth.

“I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.” John saw the kingdom, the tabernacle Christ entered into, come down from heaven. That is thy kingdom come.
“Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people, and God himself shall be with them, and be their God.” This people are the Israelites.

“God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes”. Right now we cry: he gave us the tears of affliction. Somebody getting shot, somebody killed unjustly; we see injustice everywhere. “There shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.”

“Behold, I make all things new.” “Write: for these words are true and faithful”: write it down, because it will come to pass. “It is done. I am Alpha and Omega”, “I will give unto him that is athirst of the fountain of the water of life freely.”
“He that overcometh shall inherit all things”: he that overcomes his or her own sins and the world. “And I will be his God, and he shall be my son.”

“But the fearful, and unbelieving, and the abominable, and murderers, and whoremongers, and sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars”: the fearful brothers and sisters, the unbelieving, the abominable, the whoremongers, the witches, the lying brothers and sisters, “shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone: which is the second death.”
“Come hither, I will shew thee the bride, the Lamb’s wife.” The bride is the twelve tribes of Israel. We are the Lamb’s wife.

“He carried me away in the spirit to a great and high mountain, and shewed me that great city, the holy Jerusalem, descending out of heaven from God”. This is the fourth temple. “Her light was like unto a stone most precious, even like a jasper stone, clear as crystal”.

“Had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel”: the same thing that is on the third temple. Three gates on each side, and “twelve foundations, and in them the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb.”

“The city lieth foursquare, and the length is as large as the breadth”: as long as it is wide. “Twelve thousand furlongs”: about 1,500 miles. “The length and the breadth and the height of it are equal”: 1,500 miles up, 1,500 across, 1,500 wide. It is only about 62 miles from the earth to space; this goes far beyond.

“According to the measure of a man, that is, of the angel.” Angels are larger than us, so the cubit and the furlong here are more than we think.

“The city was pure gold, like unto clear glass. And the foundations of the wall of the city were garnished with all manner of precious stones.” These are the same stones as on the ephod in Exodus 28, each stone representing one of the twelve tribes: jasper, sapphire, chalcedony, emerald, sardonyx, sardius, chrysolite, beryl, topaz, chrysoprasus, jacinth, amethyst.
“The twelve gates were twelve pearls; every several gate was of one pearl”. They say one pearly gate; it says twelve gates, because there are twelve tribes.
“And I saw no temple therein: for the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are the temple of it.”

precepts.why: How is the bride the twelve tribes? “Turn, O backsliding children, saith the Lord; for I am married unto you: and I will take you one of a city, and two of a family, and I will bring you to Zion”. God said I am married to you. He is not taking all Israelites, only the elect, one of a city and two of a family, and bringing them to Zion: that is his bride.

“For I am jealous over you with godly jealousy: for I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.” Paul espoused us to one husband, Christ. We are the Lamb’s wife.

“For the entrances of the elder world were wide and sure, and brought immortal fruit.” We are going back to the elder world: the elder world is the kingdom, paradise. “If then they that live labour not to enter these strait and vain things, they can never receive those that are laid up for them.”

“Thou hast ordained in thy law, that the righteous should inherit these things, but that the ungodly should perish. Nevertheless the righteous shall suffer strait things, and hope for wide”. We are going to suffer hard things, affliction, and hope for the wide: the kingdom. “For they that have done wickedly have suffered the strait things, and yet shall not see the wide.” Our people who have done wickedly suffer too, and will not see immortality, the kingdom. That is overcoming to inherit all things.

“I commanded thee to go into the field, where no foundation of any building was. For in the place wherein the Highest beginneth to shew his city, there can no man’s building be able to stand.” No man’s building stands when the kingdom comes; all kingdoms must fall.

“Go thy way in, and see the beauty and greatness of the building, as much as thine eyes be able to see”. As much as your eyes can see, because it is 1,500 miles up and 1,500 miles wide; your eyes can hardly see that far. What the angel told Ezra is what John revealed to us through Christ.

“For thou art blessed above many other, and art called with the Highest; and so are but few.” Only a few are going to be saved: the 144,000 and that multitude.
